rationale:
Metal Slug Tactics register played straight: 3.4-head chibi proportions (18px head on a 62px figure), unbroken plum-black ink contour around every gear piece, flat clustered shading at two values per material with a sparse third band reserved for metal and the pale cross, and a deliberately oversized weapon. 24 colours. Identity budget is roughly 70% grey-teal coat / 25% rust livery / 5% teal emission, anchored on #120b10; no magenta, no chartreuse.

The design solves the rejection by inverting where the detail sits. The head is the widest single element in the figure (24px at the brim, wider than the shoulders at 20px) and carries the only true highlight values in the palette, so the eye lands there first. Everything below it is deliberately quieter: the torso is a plain coat slab whose only event is the rust chest panel with a bone cross, and the arms are three-value chains (rust sleeve, metal cuff, dark glove) that separate from the body via 2px transparent gaps rather than via internal detail.

Personality comes from asymmetry rather than from a twisted pose, which does not survive 48px. The left arm hangs down-and-out into an oversized injector-cannon, a 12x13 dark metal mass with a teal ampoule that reads as a heavy weapon rather than a prop; the right arm angles outward through a metal cuff into a big hanging glove. Legs are staggered so the viewer-right boot lands three rows higher than the left, with rust thigh pouches at different heights on each leg. Light is upper-left throughout: an 'e' rim light runs down the left edge of coat, legs, and boots, and 'C' shadow falls right.

What it sacrifices: a genuinely dynamic action pose. I tried a raised-weapon chicken-wing arm and a cross-body reach in intermediate iterations; both collapsed into unreadable blobs at this resolution because a doubling-back limb needs a visible negative-space crook that costs more pixels than are available. The figure therefore reads as planted and ready rather than mid-action. It also spends most of its silhouette budget on the head and the weapon, leaving the torso plain.
frontFacingCue:
A four-band value stack down the head that cannot be produced by the back of a skull. Reading top to bottom: dark helmet dome (#2d3738), then a rust brim (#a8503a) that juts two pixels wider than the crown on both sides, then a hard ink line under the brim, then the brightest band in the entire sprite - twin goggle lenses in #ece0cf and #bccbc7 with a dark bridge between them - then a lit skin face plane with a 2-3px nose shadow running down the centre, then a 6px ink mouth, then a jaw that tapers over three rows to a chin, then a #6d3b31 under-chin shadow, then a 6px-wide skin neck flanked by transparency.

Two things enforce the separation from the shoulders specifically. First, the neck is a real 2-row, 6px column of lit skin that is 14px narrower than the head above it and 24px narrower than the shoulders below it, with transparent pixels on both sides, so the down-looking dimetric camera cannot swallow it. Second, nothing rises above the shoulder line at all - there is no pack, no hood, no collar peak; the highest non-head element is the coat collar at row 21, three rows below the chin. The single teal pixel pair at the collar centre reads as a front-mounted status light, reinforcing which side is which.
smallCheck:
Yes, it survives, with two honest losses. I box-downscaled to 28px tall (21x28) and inspected at 8x. What holds: the head silhouette with its wide brim, the goggle band as a bright horizontal slash, the pale face beneath it, the rust shoulder caps as two distinct orange blocks, the chest cross as a light smudge on rust, and the injector-cannon as a dark diagonal with a legible teal glint at lower-left. The front-facing read survives intact, which is the requirement that matters most - at 28px the goggle-band-over-face-over-neck stack is still three distinguishable bands.

What is lost: the leg articulation collapses. Even after I widened the inter-leg gap from 1px to 2px and added an #6d7c77 rim light down the left edge of each leg and boot, the lower half reads as a single dark mass with only a faint vertical split, and the staggered boot heights stop registering. The right glove also merges into the torso silhouette. The pouches, wear chips, and belt detail disappear entirely, as expected.

If 28px is the shipping size, I would cut the sprite differently rather than rely on this one: shorten the legs by four rows, push the gap to 3px, and lighten the pant base a further two steps. At the authored 48x64 and at any integer scale of it, none of this is a concern.
